title: The Globe Of The Earth Its Journey And The Proofs Of Mercy On The Page Of Spring

questions.question: What does the globe invite the traveler to do first?
questions.answer: It invites him to look at its works and learn from what it shows.

questions.question: What two places is the traveler told he does not need to keep wandering through?
questions.answer: He is told not to keep searching through the sky and outer space.

questions.question: What comparison is used to describe the globe’s movement?
questions.answer: It is compared to a whirling dervish turning in a lively way.

questions.question: What comes from the globe’s two kinds of motion?
questions.answer: They bring about the order of days, years, and seasons.

questions.question: How is the earth pictured as a ship?
questions.answer: It is described as a huge ship carrying the supplies and nourishment needed by living creatures.

questions.question: Where is this great ship said to be traveling?
questions.answer: It is traveling through space while circling the sun.

questions.question: What does the traveler notice when he looks at the earth like a book?
questions.answer: He sees that its pages and sections point again and again to the Lord of the earth.

questions.question: Which page of the earth does he study more closely?
questions.answer: He studies the page of spring and the bringing forth of living things in that season.

questions.question: What is amazing about how many living forms appear in spring?
questions.answer: Very many kinds of living things come out from simple matter with great exactness.

questions.question: What happens to some seeds in a remarkable way?
questions.answer: Some are given means to travel through the air so they can spread to other places.

questions.question: How are these seeds and young living things treated after they appear?
questions.answer: They are distributed, fed, and raised with great care.

questions.question: From what simple sources does the passage say many foods are produced?
questions.answer: They come from dry soil, roots, seeds, and tiny drops of fluid that seem very similar.

questions.question: What picture is used for the arrival of food and supplies every spring?
questions.answer: It is pictured as goods being loaded from an unseen storehouse onto a rail car and sent out in perfect order.

questions.question: What example is given to show special mercy toward babies?
questions.answer: Babies are provided ready nourishment, especially milk through their mothers in a loving and wise way.

questions.question: What big truth does the page of spring show according to the passage?
questions.answer: It shows signs of Allah’s mercy by bringing dead earth back to life and pointing to resurrection.

questions.question: How does spring support belief in life after death?
questions.answer: The return of life across the earth each year is presented as a clear example that reviving the dead is possible.

questions.question: What conclusion does the traveler reach from all the earth’s pages?
questions.answer: He understands that all of them declare Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: Why does the globe speak to the traveler in the passage?
questions.answer: It wants to show him what he has been searching for.

questions.question: Instead of searching far away, what is he told to examine?
questions.answer: He is told to study the earth’s functions and signs.

questions.question: What does the globe’s turning help organize in human life?
questions.answer: It organizes time through the pattern of days, years, and seasons.

questions.question: What does the earth carry for living things?
questions.answer: It carries many kinds of provisions and necessary materials for all creatures.

questions.question: What does the earth’s steady movement in space suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests careful balance and control.

questions.question: How does the traveler describe the earth after looking at it closely?
questions.answer: He sees it like a book full of signs pointing to its Sustainer.

questions.question: Why does he focus on spring instead of everything on earth?
questions.answer: The whole earth is too much to take in at once, so he studies one page more closely.

questions.question: What does the phrase about countless species appearing from simple material teach?
questions.answer: It teaches that great variety can be brought out from something basic and plain with precision.

questions.question: What does the spreading of seeds through the air show?
questions.answer: It shows wise planning in how plant life is multiplied and sent to where it is needed.

questions.question: What do careful feeding and nurturing of living things suggest?
questions.answer: They suggest mercy, attention, and ongoing care.

questions.question: Why is it important that many foods come from sources that look very similar?
questions.answer: It shows that very different and useful results can come from simple and similar beginnings.

questions.question: What does the image of spring supplies coming from an unseen treasury mean?
questions.answer: It means the earth receives rich provision from a source beyond what people can directly see.

questions.question: How does the example of milk for infants strengthen the message of the passage?
questions.answer: It gives a close, human example of loving care, wisdom, and mercy.

questions.question: What season is presented as a living proof of mercy?
questions.answer: Spring is presented as a living proof of mercy.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does reviving the earth after winter point to?
questions.answer: It points to the power to raise the dead back to life.

questions.question: What does the traveler understand about the verse mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: He understands that its meaning is clearly shown in the events of spring.

questions.question: What change in direction happens at the start of the target passage?
questions.answer: Attention shifts from searching the heavens to learning from the earth.

questions.question: What does the globe promise the traveler?
questions.answer: It promises to show him the truth he is looking for.

questions.question: How is the earth’s motion described in a way that makes it easier to imagine?
questions.answer: It is described as graceful turning like a spinning dervish.

questions.question: What results from the earth’s motion around its path?
questions.answer: The passing of time in regular patterns such as days, years, and seasons.

questions.question: Why is the earth called a grand ship?
questions.answer: Because it carries huge amounts of food and supplies for every kind of living being.

questions.question: What does the phrase about perfect balance teach about the earth’s movement?
questions.answer: It teaches that its movement is not random or chaotic.

questions.question: What literary image is used when the traveler examines the earth?
questions.answer: The earth is pictured as a book with pages and chapters to be read.

questions.question: What do the pages of that book do?
questions.answer: They announce and point to the Lord who sustains the earth.

questions.question: Which topic on the earth’s page does the traveler study?
questions.answer: He studies the coming into being and spreading of living things in spring.

questions.question: What is striking about the birth of many species in spring?
questions.answer: So many different forms appear accurately from plain material.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens to certain seeds?
questions.answer: They are given a way to travel and then spread widely.

questions.question: What does this detail suggest about the natural world?
questions.answer: It suggests order, purpose, and care in how life continues.

questions.question: What does the train-car image help the reader understand?
questions.answer: It helps the reader picture how many kinds of provisions are delivered in an organized way.

questions.question: Why is nourishment for babies given special attention?
questions.answer: Because it strongly shows gentleness, compassion, and wise planning.

questions.question: How is spring connected to the idea of the Supreme Gathering, or resurrection?
questions.answer: Spring is shown as many repeated examples of life returning after death-like stillness.

questions.question: What final message does the traveler hear from the earth as a whole?
questions.answer: He hears a witness to Allah’s oneness from all across the earth.

questions.question: How does the globe guide him toward that goal?
questions.answer: It tells him to study the earth itself and learn from its works.

questions.question: What does the earth’s double motion produce?
questions.answer: It produces the repeating order of day, year, and season.

questions.question: What does the earth carry besides living creatures?
questions.answer: It carries the nourishment and tools they need to live.

questions.question: What does floating in space with balance suggest about the earth?
questions.answer: It suggests that it is kept in a stable and measured condition.

questions.question: What does the traveler realize about the earth’s pages?
questions.answer: He realizes they are full of signs that teach about the Sustainer.

questions.question: Which part of the earth’s “book” does he focus on?
questions.answer: He focuses on springtime life.

questions.question: What happens to many species in spring?
questions.answer: Their forms appear in large numbers and with exact design.

questions.question: How are some seeds helped to spread?
questions.answer: They are given features that let them travel through the air.

questions.question: What three kinds of care are mentioned for living things after they appear?
questions.answer: They are spread out well, provided for, and raised carefully.

questions.question: What does the wide variety of foods coming from similar small beginnings show?
questions.answer: It shows wisdom and power in creation.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention roots, seeds, and tiny drops?
questions.answer: To show that very rich and different provisions can come from very simple beginnings.

questions.question: What does the unseen treasury image teach about provision in spring?
questions.answer: It teaches that spring’s blessings come from a hidden source of mercy and power.

questions.question: How does a mother feeding her baby serve as a sign in the passage?
questions.answer: It serves as a clear sign of tenderness, generosity, and thoughtful care.

questions.question: What lesson does the revival of the earth after death-like stillness teach?
questions.answer: It teaches that the One who restores life to the earth can also raise the dead.

questions.question: After reflecting on spring, what testimony does the traveler understand from the earth?
questions.answer: He understands that the earth declares that there is no god but Allah.

questions.question: What invitation begins the target passage?
questions.answer: The earth invites the traveler to stop roaming above and learn from the earth itself.

questions.question: What does the globe want the traveler to read?
questions.answer: It wants him to read its pages, meaning its signs and functions.

questions.question: What image helps describe the globe’s motion in a lively way?
questions.answer: The image of a spinning dervish.

questions.question: What regular cycles come from this motion?
questions.answer: The cycles of days, years, and seasons.

questions.question: How is the earth both moving and serving at the same time?
questions.answer: It travels through space while carrying what living things need.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the earth’s balance in space?
questions.answer: It says the earth moves with complete steadiness and balance.

questions.question: What does each page of the earth announce?
questions.answer: Each page announces the One who sustains and governs it.

questions.question: Why does the traveler not examine every page in detail?
questions.answer: Because there is too much to read all at once.

questions.question: What does he choose to study as an example?
questions.answer: He chooses the springtime appearance and spreading of living beings.

questions.question: How do countless living forms begin, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They begin from simple material but appear with great care and exactness.

questions.question: What special gift is given to some seeds?
questions.answer: They are given the ability to travel and spread.

questions.question: What does this spreading tell us about nature in the passage?
questions.answer: It tells us that life is arranged with purpose and wisdom.

questions.question: What kind of foods are produced from the earth?
questions.answer: Many delicious and beneficial foods are produced.

questions.question: What comparison is used for the delivery of spring provisions?
questions.answer: It is compared to loading supplies onto a wagon and sending them out in order.

questions.question: Why is milk for infants such a strong example in the passage?
questions.answer: Because it shows loving care prepared exactly for a baby’s need.

questions.question: What does spring show besides plant and animal life?
questions.answer: It shows signs of mercy and a sample of resurrection.

questions.question: What does the traveler finally understand the whole earth is saying?
questions.answer: He understands that it is calling people to Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What does the globe tell the traveler about his search?
questions.answer: It tells him that what he seeks can be known by looking at the earth.

questions.question: What does “read my pages” mean in this passage?
questions.answer: It means to study the signs, works, and patterns found in the earth.

questions.question: How is the earth’s motion described so that a student can picture it?
questions.answer: It is pictured as a turning figure moving in a graceful circle.

questions.question: What time patterns are linked to the earth’s movement?
questions.answer: Day and night, the years, and the seasons.

questions.question: What makes the earth like a giant ship?
questions.answer: It carries huge amounts of provisions for all living things.

questions.question: Around what does the earth travel in the passage?
questions.answer: It travels around the sun.

questions.question: What does the traveler discover when he examines the earth like a text?
questions.answer: He discovers many signs pointing to the Sustainer of the earth.

questions.question: Which “page” receives special attention?
questions.answer: The page of spring.

questions.question: What appears in spring from simple material?
questions.answer: The forms of many living species appear.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the precision of these forms?
questions.answer: Their creation is purposeful, wise, and carefully arranged.

questions.question: What role do flying seeds play in the passage?
questions.answer: They help spread plant life to many places.

questions.question: How are living things supported after they appear?
questions.answer: They are provided for and raised with mercy and care.

questions.question: What is surprising about the sources of many foods?
questions.answer: They come from plain and similar things, yet produce many different benefits.

questions.question: What does the hidden storehouse image suggest about springtime blessings?
questions.answer: It suggests that these blessings are sent by Allah from beyond what people can see.

questions.question: How does the example of mothers feeding babies deepen the message?
questions.answer: It shows mercy in a tender form people can easily recognize.

questions.question: Why is the verse about bringing dead earth back to life important here?
questions.answer: It matches what the traveler sees in spring and points to Allah’s power over resurrection.

questions.question: What overall statement does the earth make through all its pages?
questions.answer: It bears witness that Allah alone is God.
